newsitem.title: POLAND: PILKINGTON TO SHED 350 JOBS IN POLAND.
newsitem.headline: PILKINGTON TO SHED 350 JOBS IN POLAND.

text.p: The Polish float-glass factory Pilkington Sandoglass sp z o.o. plans to shed 350 out of the 1,280 jobs in line with the 1993 deal with the Polish government, general director of the firm said.

Pilkington Sandoglass is 40-percent owned by British Pilkington Plc, the World Bank's International Finance Corporation and New East European Investment Fund have 15 percent stakes each, and the state treasury 30 percent.
"About a quarter of the present workforce is going to be laid off," Jonas Borup told Reuters.
Borup said the move was partly connected to closing an unprofitable department of the factory producing insulating glass, employing 50, but said the main reason of the sacking was overmanning.
Borup also said, Pilkington wanted to expand its activities in Poland by opening a new factory in a year and a half.
"It's going to produce automotive glass, windscreens and other car glasses and we will have to reemploy some people," he said.
He said the new factory was likely to be based also in Sandomierz, south-eastern Poland, and to employ 220 people in the first stage, which later would be increased to 320.
